description:
# FastEdit

Async WorldEdit-style plugin for PowerNukkitX (Minecraft Bedrock servers).
Wand, brushes, schematics, undo/redo — without the lag.

---

## Install

Requires **PowerNukkitX 3.0.x** (plugin API `3.0.0`). For PNX 2.x servers, stay
on FastEdit 1.0.5.

1. Drop `FastEdit-1.3.0.jar` into your server's `plugins/` folder.
2. Restart the server.
3. In-game: `//wand` to get the wooden axe.

That's it. No config file, no permissions to set up (commands default to op).

> Every command works with both syntaxes: `/wand` *and* `//wand`. The double
> slash is rewritten to single slash transparently, so muscle-memory from
> Java's WorldEdit still works.

---

## Quick start

```
//wand              # gives you the FastEdit wooden axe
[left-click]        # sets position 1 on the clicked block
[right-click]       # sets position 2
//size              # shows the size of your selection
//set stone         # fills it with stone
//undo              # changed your mind
```

You can also stand somewhere and use `//pos1` / `//pos2` instead of the wand.

---

## Selecting

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `//wand` | Get the wooden axe. Break = pos1, right-click = pos2. |
| `//pos1` | Set pos1 to your current block. |
| `//pos2` | Set pos2 to your current block. |
| `//sel` | Show the current selection. |
| `//sel clear` | Clear it. |
| `//size` | Show width × height × length and the block count. |
| `//expand <n> [dir]` | Grow the selection (see below). |
| `//expandrod` | Get the blaze rod that grows it by clicking. |

---

## Building shapes

Everything below operates on your current selection (or for `//sphere`,
`//cyl`, `//pyramid`, at your feet):

```
//set <pattern>                          fill the selection
//replace <mask> <pattern>               replace blocks matching the mask
//walls <pattern>                        outer walls of the selection
//sphere <pattern> <radius> [hollow]     sphere at your feet
//cyl <pattern> <radius> <height> [hollow]
//pyramid <pattern> <size> [hollow]
```

Examples:

```
//set oak_planks
//set 70%stone,30%cobblestone            ~70% stone, ~30% cobble
//replace dirt grass_block               only swap dirt blocks
//replace #air glass                     fill air with glass
//walls bricks
//sphere glowstone 6
//cyl water 4 12 hollow                  hollow water cylinder
//pyramid sandstone 8
```

### Patterns

What you write as `<pattern>`:

| Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stone` | a single block |
| `minecraft:stone` | same, fully qualified |
| `50%stone,50%dirt` | weighted random |
| `stone,dirt,grass_block` | equal-weight random |
| `oak_stairs[weirdo_direction=2]` | a specific block state |

### Orientation is kept

Stairs, slabs, logs, trapdoors, doors, walls and everything else that has a
facing keep it when you replace them. `//replace oak_stairs stone_brick_stairs`
swaps the material and leaves every step pointing the way it already did,
upside-down ones included — it does **not** flatten the whole staircase into
the default east-facing state.

It works across block families too, through whatever property each one uses
for the same idea:

```
//replace oak_stairs stone_brick_stairs   facing + upside-down carried over
//replace cobblestone_slab oak_slab       top/bottom half carried over
//replace oak_log birch_log               axis carried over
//replace oak_stairs oak_slab             an upside-down stair becomes a top slab
//replace wooden_door iron_door           facing, hinge, open, upper half
```

To *set* an orientation instead of inheriting it, spell it out — anything you
write by hand wins over the old block:

```
//set oak_log[pillar_axis=y]                        stand every log upright
//replace oak_stairs oak_stairs[weirdo_direction=0] point them all east
```

`/inspect` (right-click a block) now prints the block's full state — exactly
the form a pattern takes, so you can paste it straight back. An unknown
property name is reported with the list of the real ones.

### Masks

What you write as `<mask>` (e.g. for `//replace`):

| Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `*` | any block |
| `#air` | only air |
| `#solid` | anything that isn't air |
| `stone` | only this block |
| `stone,dirt` | any of these |
| `!stone` | anything *except* stone |
| `oak_stairs[upside_down_bit=true]` | only blocks in that state |

---

## Clipboard

```
//copy                       copy the selection (anchor = where you stand)
//cut                        same as copy, then clears the selection
//paste                      paste at your feet
//paste -noair               paste but keep existing blocks where the clip is air
//rotate <90|180|270>        rotate clipboard around Y
//flip <x|y|z>               mirror the clipboard
```

Default `//paste` *overwrites everything* in the paste box, including with
air blocks from the clipboard. Use `-noair` if you want to overlay the
clipboard on existing terrain without clearing the gaps.

---

## Move & stack

```
//move <amount> [direction]      move the selection (and update pos1/pos2)
//stack <count> [direction]      duplicate the selection N times in a row
```

`direction` is one of: `up`, `down`, `north`, `south`, `east`, `west`, or
`me` (the direction you're facing — default, including up and down).

```
//stack 5 east        copy your selection 5 times to the east
//stack 3             stack it upward/downward when looking up/down
//move 10 up          push the selection 10 blocks up
```

---

## Expand the selection

Grow your current selection without re-selecting it — same idea as Java
WorldEdit's `//expand`.

```
//expand <amount> [direction]            grow one side
//expand <amount> <reverse> [direction]  grow both opposite sides at once
//expand <amount> n,w                    several directions in one go
//expand vert                            stretch to the world's build limits
```

`direction` is the same set as `//move`: `up`, `down`, `north`, `south`,
`east`, `west`, or `me` / `back` (relative to where you're looking — `me`
is the default if you omit it, and it accounts for looking up or down).

```
//expand 10 up        raise the top of the selection by 10
//expand 5 5 up       add 5 above and 5 below
//expand 8 me         push it 8 blocks the way you're facing
//expand vert         floor-to-ceiling on the same footprint
```

### Expand rod

```
//expandrod
[click any block face]
```

`//expandrod` gives you a **blaze rod**. Left- or right-click a block and
the selection grows **1 block toward the face you clicked** — top face
grows it up, north face grows it north, and so on. Handy for nudging a
selection out by hand instead of re-typing coordinates. (You need a
selection first; set it with `//wand`, `//pos1`/`//pos2`.)

---

## Undo / Redo

```
//undo [count]        undo the last N edits (default: 1)
//redo [count]        redo
```

Each player keeps the last **20 edits** in memory. Cleared on server restart.

---

## Schematics

FastEdit reads three formats:

| Extension | Origin | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.mcstructure` | Bedrock native | The default save format. |
| `.schem` | Sponge (WorldEdit / FAWE / Axiom) | Java-edition blocks are translated. |
| `.schematic` | Legacy MCEdit | Older format; numeric IDs. |

Two folders are scanned, in this order:

- `plugins/FastEdit/schematics/` — drop your downloaded `.schem` files here
- The world's `structures/` folder — anything saved via vanilla `/structure
  save`, SimpleWorldEdit, or FastEdit's own `//schem save`

```
//schem list                 list everything FastEdit can see
//schem load <name>          load it into your clipboard
//schem save <name>          save the clipboard as .mcstructure
//paste                      drop it in the world
```

### Java → Bedrock blocks

Schematics made on Java Edition reference block names that don't always exist
on Bedrock (`minecraft:stonebrick`, `minecraft:terracotta`, `minecraft:wool`,
etc.). FastEdit translates the common ones automatically.

For anything genuinely unknown, FastEdit places **`minecraft:magenta_wool`**
as a visible placeholder and remembers the original Java ID. After pasting:

```
//paste                      "FastEdit | pasted 8421 blocks. (37 placeholders)"
/inspect                     gives you the FastEdit Inspector stick
[right-click a pink block]   shows "current: minecraft:magenta_wool"
                                  "original (Java): minecraft:stonebrick"
```

You can then fix the placeholders with a regular `//replace`:

```
//pos1 ... //pos2 ...        select the area you pasted into
//replace minecraft:magenta_wool minecraft:stone_bricks
```

The mapping is persisted to `plugins/FastEdit/unknown_blocks.dat`, so the
inspector still works after a restart.

---

## Brushes (paint with a shovel)

Brushes are stored **inside** your shovel — give different shovels different
brushes and switch between them.

```
[hold any shovel: wooden, stone, iron, golden, diamond, netherite]
//brush sphere stone 5
[right-click anywhere — even at the sky, raycast finds the block in front]
```

Available brushes:

```
//brush sphere   <pattern> <radius>
//brush cube     <pattern> <radius>
//brush cyl      <pattern> <radius> <height>
//brush smooth   <radius> [passes]
//brush clipboard [-noair]
//brush none                          unbind the brush from this shovel
```

### Smooth

```
//brush smooth 6          round off the terrain in a 6-block sphere
//brush smooth 6 3        three passes — smooths much harder
```

`//brush smooth` takes no pattern: it reuses the ground's own blocks, so grass
stays on top of dirt on top of stone instead of the whole cut turning into one
material. Water and lava close back over what it carves out, and it only writes
where the terrain actually changes — brushing already-smooth ground does
nothing at all.

It works on the full shape of the land rather than one height per column, so
caves and overhangs survive, and a flat floor or a straight wall is left
exactly where it is. Trees and plants are ignored when reading the terrain, so
brushing a forested hillside follows the hill and not the trunks.

`passes` (default `2`, max `6`) is how hard to smooth: 1 nudges a bumpy
surface, 4 melts a cliff into a slope. Radius is capped at 32.

Add a mask so the brush only affects matching blocks:

```
//brush sphere stone 6
//mask #air                           only paint into air
//mask !bedrock                       paint anywhere except on bedrock
//mask none                           clear the mask
```

Right-click triggers a brush stroke. There's a **500 ms cooldown** to prevent
spam from Bedrock's hold-to-attack behaviour, and the raycast reaches up to
256 blocks so you can sculpt from a distance.

---

## Inspector

```
/inspect
[right-click a block]
```

Shows the block's coordinates, its current ID, and — if it's a placeholder
from a schematic load — its original Java ID. Useful for cleaning up
schematics that referenced Bedrock-unknown blocks.

---

## All commands at a glance

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `//wand` | Give the wooden axe |
| `//pos1` `//pos2` | Set positions manually |
| `//sel [clear]` | Show / clear the selection |
| `//size` | Show selection volume |
| `//expand <n> [rev] [dir]` `//expand vert` | Grow the selection |
| `//expandrod` | Blaze rod: click a face to grow the selection |
| `//set <pat>` | Fill |
| `//replace <mask> <pat>` | Conditional fill |
| `//walls <pat>` | Outline |
| `//sphere <pat> <r> [hollow]` | Sphere at your feet |
| `//cyl <pat> <r> <h> [hollow]` | Cylinder |
| `//pyramid <pat> <size> [hollow]` | Pyramid |
| `//copy` `//cut` `//paste [-noair]` | Clipboard |
| `//rotate <90\|180\|270>` `//flip <x\|y\|z>` | Transform clipboard |
| `//move <n> [dir]` `//stack <n> [dir]` | Move / stack |
| `//undo [n]` `//redo [n]` | Undo / redo |
| `//schem <save\|load\|list> [name]` | Schematics |
| `//brush <kind> <args>` `//mask <mask>` | Brushes |
| `/inspect` | Block info stick |

---

## Under the hood

A short note for the curious — you don't need any of this to use the plugin.

- **Async planning, sliced apply.** Block coordinates are computed on a
  virtual thread (no main-thread cost), then written on the main thread in
  60 000-block slices per tick, so the server keeps a healthy TPS even on
  huge edits.
- **Batched writes.** Each tick's slice goes through PowerNukkitX's
  `BlockManager.applySubChunkUpdate()`, which sends one packet per sub-chunk
  instead of one per block and writes chunks in parallel.
- **No physics / redstone updates** are triggered by edits — exactly the
  behaviour world-edit operations expect.
- **Per-player session** keeps pos1, pos2, the clipboard, and a 20-deep
  undo/redo stack in memory.

The full architecture lives in
`src/main/java/fr/fastedit/edit/EditEngine.java` if you want to read it.

---

## Building from source

The compile classpath is a local PowerNukkitX 3 build — the plain jar *and*
its dependency jars, which is exactly what `./gradlew shadowJar` leaves in
PNX's own `build/libs/`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/PowerNukkitX/PowerNukkitX.git ../PowerNukkitX
(cd ../PowerNukkitX && ./gradlew shadowJar -PbuildVersion=3.0.1)

./gradlew shadowJar
# produces build/libs/FastEdit-1.3.0.jar
```

A sibling `../PowerNukkitX/build/libs` is picked up automatically; point
somewhere else with:

```bash
FASTEDIT_PNX_JAR=/path/to/pnx/build/libs ./gradlew shadowJar
```

---

## License

MIT. Do whatever you want with it.
name: FastEdit

versions.changelog:
Two fixes: `//replace` was throwing away a block's orientation, and the `smooth` brush wrecked the terrain instead of smoothing it.

## Orientation is kept

A pattern token resolved to the block type's **default state**. So `//replace oak_stairs stone_brick_stairs` did swap the material, but put every step back facing east and right side up — a whole staircase turned into a pile of blocks all pointing the same way. Same for slabs (top/bottom), logs (axis), trapdoors and doors.

`BlockStates.reorient` now replays the old block's properties onto the new one, in two passes:

1. **Same name on both sides**: straight copy. Covers stairs→stairs, slabs→slabs, logs→logs, and the whole family.
2. **Different names for the same idea**: through a canonical `BlockFace` / vertical half / axis. Bedrock spells the same orientation six different ways depending on the block — `weirdo_direction` for stairs, `minecraft:vertical_half` for slabs, `direction` for trapdoors, `minecraft:cardinal_direction` for doors, `facing_direction` for pistons, `pillar_axis` for logs.

```
//replace oak_stairs stone_brick_stairs   facing + upside-down carried over
//replace cobblestone_slab oak_slab       top/bottom half carried over
//replace oak_log birch_log               axis carried over
//replace oak_stairs oak_slab             an upside-down stair becomes a top slab
//replace wooden_door iron_door           facing, hinge, open, upper half
```

A PNX API trap along the way: `BlockState` compares `BlockPropertyType` by **identity**, never by name. A value built from a `CommonBlockProperties` constant is rejected as soon as the block was registered with another instance of the same name — `rail_direction` exists as both 0-9 and 0-5. Values are therefore always created from the **target** block's own `getPropertyTypeSet()`.

### Explicit states

Patterns and masks now take `id[prop=value,...]`. That is the way out: anything written by hand is pinned and never overwritten by the old block.

```
//set oak_log[pillar_axis=y]                        stand every log upright
//replace oak_stairs oak_stairs[weirdo_direction=0] point them all east
//replace oak_stairs[upside_down_bit=true] oak_slab  only the flipped ones
```

An unknown property is reported with the list of the real ones, and `/inspect` prints the block's full state — exactly the form a pattern takes, so it can be pasted straight back.

Zero cost on blocks with no properties: `//set stone` does no extra world read, and that is decided once when the pattern is parsed.

## The smooth brush, rewritten

The old one averaged **one height per column**, then re-poured the whole column from a pattern. Consequences: overhangs and caves were shaved into a single surface, everything it touched came out in the brush's material whatever the rock was, and it rewrote its entire cylinder even where the terrain was already smooth.

Redone on the model of EasyEdit's [`SmoothTask`](https://github.com/platz1de/EasyEdit). Each column of the window becomes a **signed distance field**: `+1` on the outermost ground block growing inwards, `-1` on the air touching it growing outwards. Blurring that field over the 3×3 neighbouring columns and re-thresholding it into ground/air is what actually rounds a surface off — spikes lose the vote, pits get filled, and flat ground or a straight wall does not move by a single block.

- **Only cells whose depth changes are written.** Brushing already-smooth terrain now does nothing at all.
- **The material comes from the column itself**, at the matching depth: grass stays on top of dirt on top of stone, instead of the whole cut turning into one block.
- **Water and lava close back** over what is carved out, instead of leaving a dry hole in a lake.
- **Trees and plants are transparent** to the height field, so the brush follows the hill and not the trunks.
- **Overhangs and caves survive**: it is the full shape of the column that is described, not a single top.

One deliberate deviation from EasyEdit: it clamps the air side of the field to a flat `-1` while letting the ground side grow, which drags material out of any wall taller than the brush. The two sides are symmetric here — verified: a vertical cliff produces no change at all.

```
//brush smooth 6          rounds the terrain off in a 6-block sphere
//brush smooth 6 4        four passes, melts a cliff into a slope
```

`//brush smooth` no longer takes a pattern, the radius comes first. A pattern typed out of habit is accepted and dropped, and shovels bound by a previous version keep working. `passes` defaults to 2, 6 maximum; the radius is capped at 32.

Bedrock detail: the numeric form needs its own command overload, otherwise the client refuses the radius where the block enum used to be.

## Also in this version

The selection outline goes through `BoxShape` primitives (PR #1 from [@ValresMC](https://github.com/ValresMC)), and `//stack` with no direction stacks up or down depending on where you look.

Still PNX 3.0.x. No change to selections, clipboard or schematics.

versions.changelog:
The selection outline drowned its own owner's connection in particle packets, far enough to drop the client on **timeout** — with no server-side error at all, since the server only ever sends.

Every point of the outline costs one `SpawnParticleEffectPacket`: there is no way to batch them, and they all leave in the same tick. The `MAX_POINTS = 600` ceiling was not one:

- the step was floored at `0.5` block, so on a small or medium selection the number of points was bounded by the perimeter alone, never by the ceiling;
- every edge emitted its end point **on top of** the budget, so 12 points were systematically out of quota.

A 5×8×5 selection sent 156 packets in one tick every 10 ticks, i.e. 312 packets/s for a single player. Past 32³ it plateaued at ~1,224 packets/s.

**Fixes**

- Step from `0.5` → `1.0` block, WorldEdit CUI's density. The outline stays readable and the count is halved.
- Budget from 600 → 160, and **actually enforced**: it is decremented edge by edge and only counts particles that were really sent, points dropped by distance costing nothing.
- The 12 edge end points are taken out of the budget **before** it is spread over the perimeter. Without that, the spread landed just above the ceiling and the last edge got cut — a box missing a side.

**Measured**

| selection | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 5×8×5 | 312 packets/s | 168 |
| 32×32×32 | 1,224 | 312 |
| 256×128×256 | 1,224 | 320 |

Worst case goes from ~1,224 to 320 packets/s per player, and the ceiling now holds for every selection size instead of only the very large ones.

`PERIOD_TICKS` stays at 10: the endrod particle lives long enough for the outline to look continuous at that rate, and stretching it further would make it blink.

No editing change: same commands, same selections, same schematics. Still PNX 3.0.x.
versions.name: FastEdit 1.2.1

versions.changelog:
Every command and every tool is now **operator-only**. Until now FastEdit declared no permission at all: any player could run `//set` or `//paste`, and the command map dispatched without a single check.

One permission, `fastedit.use`, declared in `plugin.yml` with `default: op`.

- **Commands** — the `FeCommand` constructor carries the permission, so all 28 commands are covered at once. `SimpleCommandMap` refuses the dispatch before execution, and `getDataForPlayer` returns `null` for a non-op: the commands no longer even appear in the Bedrock client's autocomplete. `execute()` re-tests the permission for callers that would not go through the command map. The `//x` aliases go through `Server.executeCommand`, so they get the same check.
- **Tools** — `WandListener` takes the same gate. The axe, the brushes, the inspector and the expand rod carry the same power as the commands without going through them: a brush handed to a player bypassed the permission outright.

Intended side effect: a non-op player can break blocks with a wooden axe again. The listener used to cancel the break for anyone holding an axe, op or not.

To open FastEdit up to a non-op rank (a builder role, for instance), granting it `fastedit.use` is enough.

No editing change: same commands, same selections, same schematics. Still PNX 3.0.x.
versions.name: FastEdit 1.2.0

versions.changelog:
Port to **PowerNukkitX 3.0.1**. 3.0 renamed the whole `cn.nukkit.*` namespace to `org.powernukkitx.*` and handed the protocol and NBT over to CloudburstMC: 1.0.5 no longer loads at all on it, every import pointing at a class that is gone.

**This version requires PNX 3.0.x. For a PNX 2.x server, stay on 1.0.5.**

What actually moved, beyond the rename:

- **Block updates** — `UpdateSubChunkBlocksPacket` is now the Cloudburst packet (setters instead of a positional constructor, list getters instead of public fields) and `BlockChangeEntry` takes a `Vector3i`, a `BlockDefinition` and an `ActorBlockSyncMessageId`. `FLAG_ALL` became a `Set<Flag>`, so the per-entry mask is rebuilt from the enum to keep exactly `NEIGHBORS|NETWORK`.
- **Command completion** — `CommandParamType` comes from the protocol library and no longer has `STRING`: `ID` carries the text parameter, as in PNX's own native commands.
- **NBT files** — `NBTIO` is gone. `NbtFiles` bridges Cloudburst streams and PNX's `CompoundTag`, the way `StructureAPI` does, keeping both formats the plugin depends on: big-endian for `unknown_blocks.dat` and little-endian for `.mcstructure`. A 971-entry `unknown_blocks.dat` written by 1.0.5 reads back identically.
- **Item NBT** — `hasCompoundTag`/`getNamedTag`/`setNamedTag` became `hasNbt`/`getNbt`/`setNbt`.
- `plugin.yml` declares `api: 3.0.0` — the `PluginManager` refuses a different major.

Verified on a 3.0.1 server: the plugin enables, both listeners register, and a command dispatches.

No in-game behaviour change: same commands, same selections, same schematics.
versions.name: FastEdit 1.1.0

versions.changelog:
Schematic paste fix: the `facing` orientation of trapdoors and several rotatable blocks was lost in the Java→Bedrock conversion, which placed them in their default state.

`JavaStates` only translated `facing` through `weirdo_direction`, `minecraft:cardinal_direction` and `facing_direction`. Trapdoors — and the whole bed/bell/cocoa/grindstone/loom/chiseled_bookshelf/beehive/decorated_pot/tripwire_hook family — carry the integer `direction` property instead, which was never filled in.

Added a `direction` branch with its two conventions (checked against PowerNukkitX and dragonfly): EWSN for trapdoors (E0 W1 S2 N3), horizontal index for the rest (S0 W1 N2 E3). No rotation needed either way.
versions.name: FastEdit 1.0.5

versions.changelog:
## FastEdit v1.0.3

  ### New
  - **`//expand`** — grow your selection without re-selecting, like Java WorldEdit:
    - `//expand <amount> [direction]`
    - `//expand <amount> <reverse> [direction]` — both sides at once
    - `//expand <amount> n,w` — several directions
    - `//expand vert` — floor-to-ceiling on the same footprint

    Direction defaults to where you're looking (up/down included).
  - **`//expandrod`** — a blaze rod; left/right-click a block face to grow
    the selection 1 block that way. Never damages the world.

  ### Schematic conversion
  More Java blocks convert instead of becoming the magenta placeholder:
  `bricks`, `chain`, water/lava/powder-snow cauldrons, potted azalea, and
  `light` (now level-accurate, 0–15). Reload affected schematics to apply.
versions.name: FastEdit 1.0.3

versions.changelog:
Major schematic-paste stability fixes plus in-game quality of life.

  ## ✨ New

  - **Unlimited paste size**: large schematics stream in bounded segments
    (constant memory regardless of size — no more OOM). `BLOCKS_PER_TICK`
    raised to 40k (~800k blocks/s, TPS stays stable).
  - **Whole-structure undo**: a single `//undo` reverts the entire paste
    at once (transactional). `//undo N` = N structures. `//redo` likewise.
  - **In-game autocomplete (Bedrock)**: native argument suggestions —
    full block list (`//set`, `//replace`, `//sphere`, `//cyl`,
    `//pyramid`, `//walls`, `//brush`, `//mask`), paste flags
    (`-noair`/`--skip-air`), sub-commands (`//schem save|load|list`),
    directions, axes, etc.

  ## 🐛 Fixes

  - **`.schem`/`.schematic` pasted as magenta or crashed**:
    - Hidden `null` error → real stack traces in console.
    - `UnknownBlocks` rewrote the file to disk per block → stall/OOM.
    - Lost orientations: Java→Bedrock state translation (stairs, slabs,
      logs, doors, trapdoors, chest/furnace facing…).
    - Legacy `.schematic`: metadata (orientation/variant/colour) now
      decoded; block-id table greatly extended.
    - Resolution **verified against the live registry**: `oak_*`→base,
      `dark_oak` signs→`darkoak`, `rooted_dirt`→`dirt_with_roots`,
      `tall_seagrass`→`seagrass`, etc. (a wrong name is skipped, never
      mis-placed).
  - **Crash loop**: an out-of-world Y block (`AIOOBE`) crashed the tick
    forever → now skipped cleanly, the poison job is dropped.
  - **Missing chunk layers**: edited chunks are now marked changed
    (persisted), relit and fully resent to players → 100% of chunks/layers
    present, even far from the player.
  - **Waterlogged blocks**: submerged stairs/fences/coral keep their water
    (Bedrock layer-1, supported in copy/cut/paste + undo).

  ## ⚠️ Known limitations

  - `waterlogged` not handled for legacy `.schematic` (pre-1.13).
  - Composite patterns (`stone,dirt`, `35:2`) are underlined client-side
    but still execute normally (no strict param tree, by design).
  - Very large pastes (>16M blocks): undo beyond the memory budget evicts
    the oldest segments (anti-crash safeguard).
  - Finalization spike at the end of very large pastes (>10k chunks).
versions.name: FastEdit 1.0.2

versions.changelog:
- EditEngine: drop BlockManager (Block allocs per write caused GC pressure /
  OOM
    on large zones). Write directly via chunk.setBlockState and ship one
    UpdateSubChunkBlocksPacket per touched sub-chunk. Add
  MAX_EDIT_SIZE=5_000_000
    guard so huge edits fail fast with a clear message instead of OOM.
  - RawNbt: minimal limit-free NBT reader to bypass PowerNukkitX's 1 MiB
    ByteArray cap; used for .schem and .schematic loading.
  - Paste defaults to overwriting (air included); -noair / --skip-air keeps
    existing terrain in air cells. Same flag for the clipboard brush.

versions.changelog:
First public release.
  
  - Wand + 23 commands (/cmd and //cmd both work)
  - Patterns + masks, async + sliced apply via BlockManager (~60k blocks/tick)
  - Clipboard (rotate/flip), paste overwrite or -noair
  - Schematics: .mcstructure / .schem (Sponge) / .schematic (legacy MCEdit)
  - Java→Bedrock aliases + magenta_wool placeholder + /inspect stick
  - Shovel-bound brushes (sphere/cube/cyl/smooth/clipboard), mask, 500 ms
  cooldown, 256-block raycast
  - Move, stack, undo/redo (20 per player)

  See README for the full guide.
